newsitem.title: INDIA: India's lower house approves 97/98 railway budget.
newsitem.headline: India's lower house approves 97/98 railway budget.

text.p: The lower house of India's parliament, the Lok Sabha, on Friday approved the railway budget for 1997/98 (April-March) by voice vote, parliament officials said.
The budget, presented by Railway Minister Ram Vilas Paswan on February 26, contained spending proposals for the railway network and revisions in freight charges and passenger fares.
The budget has to be ratified by the upper house, the Rajya Sabha. Its approval was considered a formality.
Under the budget, freight rates would be increased by 12 percent but select commodities would be exempted.
According to official estimates, the freight hike would result in a rise of 9.19 paise per litre in the price of high-speed diesel, a key fuel used in goods transport.
The freight hike would also result in increases in the cost of transporting coal (45 rupees per tonne) and cement (2.45 rupees per 50 kg). ($1 = 35.75 rupees) (1 rupee = 100 paise)
